subject: Dedicated pool levelling compact — proposal for short-term smoothing
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool levelling compact — proposal for short-term smoothing

Team,

Quick proposal for a short-term operational approach Im calling the "levelling compact" — we expect a two-week elevated multi-tenant traffic spike tied to a partner joint-campaign (Orion Health). We need a way to smooth impact across Dedicated pools without changing long-term commitments or doing heavy infra churn. High-level asks:

- Tech: Can we implement a temporary smoothing policy on a per-pool basis (see bullets below)?
- Ops: Runbook updates and a 72-hour rollback plan if SLOs degrade.
- Sales/Finance: Confirm whether reduced concurrency caps would trigger any reserved capacity credits for affected customers.

Proposal summary (rough):
- Window: 2026-09-15 00:00 UTC -> 2026-09-29 23:59 UTC (14 days)
- Scope: dedi-us-east-1 pools: pool-3 and pool-5 only (non-production carve).
- Behavioral changes: apply a transient max-allocation ceiling at 85% of normal pool capacity; route best-effort background/analytics traffic to hosted inference; reduce per-tenant concurrency ceiling by 10% for non-enterprise tiers.
- Autoscaler change: switch to a smoothing aggressive smoothing factor (alpha=0.3) for the two-week window and cap burst replicas at +8 GPUs per pool.

Attachments: levelling_compact_onepager.pdf (one-pager + decision checklist).

Goal: avoid broad preemptions and keep telemetry within normal bounds while we evaluate model-serving latency under campaign load.

Please reply with feasibility notes and any clear blockers. If we can get ops + infra signoff by EOD tomorrow (2026-09-03) I will schedule the pilot run on the 15th.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool levelling compact — proposal for short-term smoothing

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear ask. A few immediate notes from infra/serving perspective:

- We cannot safely reduce min_replicas for enterprise-dedicated contracts (SLA + contractual minimums). Any change that affects min_replicas would require legal/finance sign-off and a formal concession note.
- The autoscaler supports a per-pool "smoothing factor" toggle (we can flip alpha), but capping burst replicas requires a small change to the allocation controller (low risk, ~1 day dev).
- Alternative that might be lower risk: soft throttling based on token-budget windows per-tenant during the window and diverting best-effort workloads at the router. That avoids changing min_replicas.

I'll run a quick validation with Marcus on pool-3 and pool-5 capacity models and tag ops runbook owners.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool levelling compact — proposal for short-term smoothing

Hannah / Kim / team,

I ran a quick sim overnight against current utilization curves for dedi-us-east-1 pool-3/pool-5. Attaching levelling_sims.csv (3 scenario traces: baseline, compact-cap(85%), and redirect-hosted). Summary:

- Applying the 85% cap reduces predicted 95p latency spikes by ~18% for latency-sensitive tenants and avoids evicting 3 enterprise slices in the worst case.
- Redirecting non-critical work to hosted reduces GPU token spend by ~12% at peak; however, it increases cross-service egress which we should account for.
- Autoscaler alpha adjustment to 0.3 with burst cap +8 GPUs reduced oscillation during synthetic traffic ramps in our sim.

Operational asks/risks:
1) We need a short blind period for metrics (first 24 hours) where we suppress automated scaling decisions to observe initial behavior and avoid cascading scale-downs — this is doable but requires a temporary pause in some alarms.
2) Contract impact: if we enforce per-tenant concurrency caps for any reserved customers, Sales/Finance need to confirm whether that maps to a credit/waiver.
3) Router rule to divert traffic must have a fallback to original pool if hosted-side errors > 1%.

If Ops is comfortable, I can cut a small PR to the allocation controller and a runbook snippet for the blind period. ETA: PR + QA in 36 hours.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: levelling_sims.csv (scenario traces)

Thanks all for the quick turns.

I like the levelling compact framing — it feels like a bounded, visible approach we can commit to with partners. A couple of next steps Id like to lock down:

- Hannah: please create a one-line partner-facing notice for Orion Health (Sara Patel) confirming traffic routing behavior and the exact window; we should avoid surprise for paid enterprise tenants.
- Kimberly / Marcus: please confirm whether the proposed changes require legal/contract amendments for any customer in the impacted pools — if yes, copy Legal (Ill loop them).
- Ops (Jonas): please add the blind-period snippet and rollback checklist to ops_runbook-draft.md and share the initial runbook PR by EOD 2026-09-03. Jonas, if you need a template I linked one in the Drive doc.

If we have infra + ops + legal alignment by EOD tomorrow (2026-09-03), I will approve the pilot schedule. If there are blockers, call them out in thread and Ill set a 30-minute sync.

Lauren Bishop
